doc_ai_transformers_5c6bcfb6::c0000::635.text:
Artificial Intelligence and Transformers

The Transformer architecture was introduced in 2017 in the paper "Attention Is All You Need" by Vaswani et al. at Google.

Transformers rely on the self-attention mechanism instead of recurrence, which allows efficient parallel training on large corpora.

BERT, published in 2018 by Google, is a Transformer-based encoder model for language understanding tasks.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines a retriever over trusted documents with a generator. The retriever finds evidence passages and the generator conditions on them.

Large language models such as GPT from OpenAI and models from Anthropic are often audited for factual accuracy using evidence-based verification.

Python Programming

Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language created by Guido van Rossum. The first version of Python was released in 1991.

Python supports object-oriented programming with classes, inheritance, and encapsulation. It also supports functional and procedural programming styles.

Python 1.0 was released in 1994 with functional programming tools such as lambda, map, filter, and reduce. (Note for audit testing: this passage gives a different date than the commonly cited 1991 first release; both passages are kept so the verification module can compare contradictory evidence.)

Python 3.0 was released in 2008 as a major backwards-incompatible update. Modern Python versions such as Python 3.11 and Python 3.12 focus on performance improvements.

Popular Python libraries include NumPy, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and FastAPI. FastAPI 0.100 introduced new routing features for building web APIs.

doc_retrieval_methods_9a1af4d2::c0000::9.text:
Keyword Search, Graph Retrieval, and Hybrid Ranking

BM25 ranks documents using term frequency and inverse document frequency. It matches exact query terms and is strong for technical terminology, dates, and version numbers.

A knowledge graph in Neo4j represents Documents, Chunks, Entities, and their relationships. A Chunk MENTIONS an Entity, an Entity is RELATED_TO another Entity, and an Entity APPEARS_IN a Document. Graph retrieval traverses these relationships to find supporting passages.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines ranked lists from multiple retrievers. Each chunk receives a fused score equal to the sum of 1/(k + rank) over the methods that returned it, with k set to 60 by default. Raw scores from different methods are never directly combined.

Hybrid retrieval merges Qdrant vector search, BM25 keyword search, and Neo4j graph traversal, then deduplicates by chunk ID and applies a final ranking stage.

doc_vector_search_qdrant_f7d92489::c0000.text:
Vector Search and Qdrant

A vector database stores dense embedding vectors and retrieves nearest neighbours by similarity search. Qdrant stores vectors with payload metadata including the original text chunk, title, source name, and domain.

Embeddings are generated with models such as sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2, which produces 384-dimensional vectors. Similarity is measured with cosine similarity over L2-normalised vectors.

Qdrant supports metadata filtering by domain, document ID, and source, as well as batch upserts with duplicate prevention based on stable point IDs.
